page: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal storage-optimized instance built on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The system is powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors operating at 2.8 GHz, delivering 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs with a single thread per core configuration. It is equipped with 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 1536.0 GB of DDR5 RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. Bundled storage comprises 45000 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD capacity, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded execution and data throughput. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang compilation tasks. Memory throughput is substantial, registering uncached read speeds of 871.74 GB/sec and write speeds of 403.47 GB/sec. Data infrastructure tests highlight top-tier capabilities, including 347.98 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, leading database operation scores in PassMark, and 160.54 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-core metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench remain in the mid-range tier.

Without accelerator hardware, text generation speeds for large language models remain low, making the instance impractical for generative AI token generation. However, the high density of physical ARM cores, coupled with 45 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage and 1.5 TB of DDR5 memory, yields high resource efficiency for data-heavy workloads on a per-gigabyte basis. The hardware profile is aligned with distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, search engines, real-time analytics, and high-concurrency data streaming pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal storage-optimized instance powered by 192 dedicated physical ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz. Designed without hyperthreading, it features 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio, along with 45000 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and 100 Gbps baseline networking. The server achieves top-tier performance across multi-core compute tests, uncached memory bandwidth benchmarks, Clang compilation, and high-frequency in-memory database operations such as Redis SET workloads. While single-threaded performance is mid-tier and generative AI inference is constrained by the absence of discrete GPUs, the bare-metal architecture delivers immense I/O and compute density. This profile makes the instance well suited for large distributed databases, big data analytics engines, log aggregation systems, and high-throughput data processing services.
